audit.whatIsWrong: diff reads HARD while every other difficulty signal on the page says the opposite, and four chart rows disagreed with their own why[] text.
audit.why: diffRating is 4/10, tone is #3ddc97 (the favoured green), breakdown.difficulty says 'Overall difficulty: 4/10', report[14] says 'Favoured matchup', report[7] says 'convert the favoured lane into kills' — and Illaoi wins 53.5%. HARD is the single outlier and it is the word the page prints biggest. On the chart: whys[0] and whys[1] both hand the early levels to Sion while win[0] read Skill; whys[2] and whys[3] hand levels 3-5 to Illaoi ('drowning him in tentacles', 'your tentacle burst peaks') while the rows read Sion and Skill.
audit.corrected: diff to FAV; rows 0, 2, 3 and 4 flipped in both layers as one atomic group with ratings to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and whys[5] are swapped: the Level 6 row is explained by 'Sion's first-item tank spike' and the First item row by 'Level-6 R walls Sion in tentacles'.
audit.why: The rest of the page is unambiguous about which spike belongs where — spikes[1] ('Lvl 6') is the Leap of Faith tentacle wall, spikes[2] ('1st item') is 'Sion spikes back here', and the mid block says 'your level-6 R wall punishes any shield-trade he tries. His first-item tank spike then lets him zone back.' A reader following the chart would hold the all-in through their own strongest level and force it into his.
audit.corrected: The two whys swapped back into their own rows, and the Level 6 side set to Illaoi to match spikes[1] and mid. Note this puts rows 4 and 5 opposite to packet.levelChart, which has the same inversion.

audit.whatIsWrong: Roar of the Slayer appears once, as a name in spikes[2], with none of its effects; Soul Furnace is written as a plain shield; Glory in Death is called 'revive' with no mechanics.
audit.why: Riot on Roar of the Slayer (E, 12/11/10/9/8s, 800 range): it damages, slows and 'reduces the Armor of the first enemy hit', and if it hits a minion the minion is knocked back through everything behind it. That is armour shred aimed at exactly the stat the page's boots recommendation buys, and it is his main way to poke an immobile juggernaut through a wave. Riot on Soul Furnace (W, 15/14/13/12/11s): he shields, then 'can reactivate after 3 seconds to deal Magic Damage to enemies nearby' — the shield is half of it; the delayed detonation is the part that punishes standing on him, and it scales with max Health, which Illaoi stacks. Riot on Glory in Death (P): after being killed he reanimates with rapid attacks that 'heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health' — killing him does not end the trade, and Grievous Wounds is what does.
audit.corrected: Armour shred and the 3-second Soul Furnace re-fire written into report[5], the cooldown block, dontsFull[1] and wants.foe[1]; the passive's max-HP healing tied to the Executioner's Calling line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Decimating Smash is tracked everywhere with no cooldown number.
audit.why: Decimating Smash 10/9/8/7/6s, Roar of the Slayer 12/11/10/9/8s, Soul Furnace 15/14/13/12/11s, Unstoppable Onslaught 140/100/60s, against Harsh Lesson at 4s and Test of Spirit at 16s. A sidestepped Q buys ten seconds at rank 1 — enough for the whole Illaoi pattern — and that is the concrete version of the advice the page gives vaguely.

audit.whatIsWrong: Executioner's Calling is justified as 'his healing fights your pattern', which does not say where the healing comes from.
audit.why: Sion has no lane heal in his kit — the healing is Glory in Death after he dies, and it scales off your maximum Health. That makes the anti-heal a post-kill item, not a laning one, and the timing advice changes with it.
audit.corrected: report[8] now names the revive as the heal source.

notes: Rows 4 and 5 now read Illaoi (Level 6) and Sion (First item), which is the opposite of packet.levelChart for those two stages. If the mirror (sion__illaoi.json) is audited later it must use the same two rows. The packet reports 1344 games while the brief header says 1851.
